question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=2x(t)+2y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=5x(t)+5y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Find an equation of the line in the phase space that contains all equilibrium points of the system above.
question.worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we have
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226345/assets/9d8df402a06960cd5f2e0c772a5fab345e4610cc90c7e88202dab34f2ab97e65.svg)
where ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226345/assets/58ab8470c661bcc5f0c95df2640185f95fc9733c1f4bf718ce51dba7a0b9a989.svg)

The equilibrium (fixed) points of a system $\mathbf{x}'(t) = \mathbf{f}(x,y)$ are the points for which $\mathbf{f}(x,y)=\mathbf{0}.$ So, we get the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x+2y=0 \\ 5x+5y=0\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the second equation is a multiple of the first one. So, we can disregard the second equation. 

From the first equation, we get

$$
2x+2y=0
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
2y=-2x
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
y=-x.
$$

Therefore, the equilibrium points are given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226345/assets/b9059ea5506ed372cb5b21771b177966be2c607934164b2ad16466a31d423834.svg)

This determines the line with the equation $y=-x.$
